inspections.finding: The complete vav has a heavy lower terminal with small swellings continuous with its shaft. The filled contour does not uniquely distinguish a printed vowel from ordinary terminal ink or separate competing vowel classes. Upper and lower zones were inspected; no point absence or expected conjunction reading is inferred.

Below the completed ordinary diagonal lamed terminal a narrow neck leads to a broad continuous shallow bar. Its long nearly flat lower edge and single one-pixel lug match the literal lamed patah. The true bare lamed ends without the added plateau; tsere has two rounded low tips and a waist, qamats a substantial narrow central column, and segol a substantial third lower node. Those complete competing arrangements are absent from the surviving bar contour. Ink contact alone does not disqualify the diagnostic shape. Only B7 is inserted; initial vav and every other unresolved point remain disclosed.

The two ordinary het feet and the broad lower ink band are coalesced. A lower lobe remains heavy enough that ordinary footer structure and merged point arrangements cannot be uniquely separated. Retain rather than fill a class from the word reading.

The closed samekh footer continues into a compact lower projection. A plain same-font samekh shows the ordinary footer and a literal qamats has an elongated drop, but this short saturated projection does not uniquely discriminate a single point from a short stem or coalesced multi-point class. Retain; a compact blob is not automatically hiriq.

The dalet shaft ends in a broad round lower mass. The local bare dalet in מאד has a thinner terminal, but the target mass does not preserve enough separate bar/node geometry to identify one vowel class uniquely. A single round outline could conceal merged points; no expected spelling supplies the class.

A broad flat lower group is joined directly to the vav shaft. Its surviving shape does not uniquely exclude a natural heavy terminal or competing merged vowel contours. The literal same-font shuruq-vav ordinary lower leg is a body comparison, not a vowel-class witness. Retain without treating flatness alone as patah.

The alef lower-left leg flows into a heavy horizontal base. A separate diagnostic point arrangement cannot be distinguished from its natural foot and merged ink. Retain without classifying that entire foot as a vowel.
